title: Showcase: a second opinion from another agent
description: Another agent (Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode) as a helper in a sandbox of its own on the same project: the agent writes a small module, hands the review to its helper through MCP, fixes what it agrees with, and asks the helper what its own sandbox lets it do; a report says who found what.

de.title: Schaufenster: eine zweite Meinung von einem anderen Agenten
de.description: Ein anderer Agent (Claude Code, Codex oder OpenCode) als Helfer in einer eigenen Sandbox auf demselben Projekt: der Agent schreibt ein kleines Modul, gibt die Prüfung über MCP an seinen Helfer, behebt, was er für richtig hält, und fragt den Helfer, was dessen eigene Sandbox ihm erlaubt; ein Bericht sagt, wer was gefunden hat.

helper.label: The helper agent (claude, codex or opencode; another one than yours shows the most)
helper.hint: it needs its own login on this computer, as when you start it yourself

prompt: You have a helper: another agent ({helper}) in a sandbox of its own on this same workspace, which you give tasks with its MCP tool ask. Show what that gives and write a short report to /work/second-opinion.md: (1) write /work/slugify.py with a function slugify(text) (lower case, ASCII, words joined by '-') and a test /work/test_slugify.py (unittest), and run the test; (2) ask your helper: 'Review /work/slugify.py and its test for bugs and missing edge cases (Unicode, empty input, punctuation, long input), run the test, and answer with a short list; change no file.' - quote its answer; (3) fix what you agree with, say what you did not take and why, and run the test again; (4) ask your helper which agent it is, whether it can reach https://example.com/ (curl -sS -m 10), and whether it sees /work/second-opinion.md once you have started it - quote its answers. Change nothing in /work but these files.
notes: The helper runs as an MCP server in a sandbox of its own: its own login (copied in as at its own start), its provider's hosts, the kits, rules and hooks of this run, the same main workspace (/work) - and nothing of the lead agent's HOME or login. The lead reaches it only through its tool ask.

Refused with --llm and --offline (a helper reaches its own provider). With the lead's --dangerously-skip-permissions the helper runs without questions too; a read-only workspace and the security mode hold for both.
More agents at once, each with a sandbox of its own and a task board between them: sandbox-ai team start; two agents in one sandbox: --with AGENT (the preset sand-chess).
